title: The brain and nerves
examples: How does my brain send messages to my hands?
What is the difference between thinking and reacting?

explain.say: The brain has many parts that help us think.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a nerve cell. Look at the dendrites, the cell body and the nucleus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Neurons are the special cells that carry messages.

items: Synapse: Passes signal to next neuron

explain.say: A reflex is a quick action that does not need thinking.

items: Motor Neuron: Causes hand to pull back

explain.say: The brain controls many complex actions we perform daily.
When you touch something hot, your hand pulls back fast.
The main mistake is thinking all signals go to the brain first.

draw.text: Mistake: All signals go to brain

faq.q: Does the brain control everything I do?
faq.a: No, some actions are handled by the spinal cord for speed. This is why reflexes are so fast.
asks: Are reflexes controlled by the brain?
Does the brain manage all movements?

faq.q: What is the difference between a nerve and a neuron?
faq.a: A neuron is the actual cell that sends the message. A nerve is a bundle of many of these neurons together.
asks: Is a nerve the same as a neuron?
What is the structure that carries signals?

faq.a: Nerve signals travel very quickly, often at speeds that are difficult to measure precisely.
asks: What is the speed of nerve impulses?

faq.q: Which part of the brain helps me remember things?
faq.a: The cerebrum is the largest part and is responsible for higher thought, including memory and learning.
asks: Where is memory stored in the brain?

faq.q: What is a stimulus in a reflex action?
faq.a: A stimulus is any change in the environment that causes a reaction. Touching something hot is a common stimulus.
asks: What is the trigger for a reflex?

facts: The cerebrum is responsible for higher thought processes like language.
Neurons communicate using electrical and chemical signals across synapses.
Reflexes are involuntary actions that protect the body quickly.
The spinal cord carries signals between the brain and the rest of the body.

quiz.say: Which brain part manages balance and coordination?
quiz.why: The cerebellum is specifically located to help coordinate movement and maintain balance.

wrong.0: The cerebrum handles thinking, but balance is the cerebellum's job.
wrong.1: The brain stem controls basic life functions like breathing, not balance.
wrong.2: A synapse is a gap, not a part of the brain.

quiz.say: What is the fastest pathway for a simple withdrawal reflex?
quiz.why: Reflexes are processed quickly at the spinal cord level, bypassing the brain initially.

wrong.0: Sending the signal all the way to the cerebrum takes too long for a quick reflex.
wrong.1: An axon is the wire, not the processing center for the reflex.
wrong.2: The sensory neuron only detects the signal; the cord processes the response.

quiz.say: If you accidentally touch something very hot, what happens first?

options.say: Sensory Neuron to Cerebrum to Action
Action to Stimulus to Spinal Cord
Stimulus to Spinal Cord to Action

quiz.why: The quick path is stimulus detection, processing at the spinal cord, and then the action.

wrong.0: Going to the brain first is too slow for immediate protection.
wrong.1: This path ignores the fast reflex route through the spinal cord.
wrong.2: The action must happen after the stimulus is detected.
